name: Akeju Emmanuel
missingPieces: D4 cites NDPA 2023 breach duty only generically (72-hour window, duty to notify subjects) without the load-bearing section numbers (section 40 NDPC within 72h, section 41 data-subject notice on high risk).
feedback: D1 is excellent and effectively complete. Akeju catalogues all ten real findings with the correct OWASP class, a defensible CWE, and a quoted evidence line for each: SQLi by string concatenation (A03/CWE-89), unsalted MD5 (A02/CWE-916), the alg:none verify branch (A07/CWE-347), the hard-coded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (CWE-798), missing exp/nbf (CWE-613), stored XSS with the cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443, XXE file:///etc/passwd, path traversal on files/?path=, open redirect via ?next=, and the insecure cookie flags. The reflected-XSS extra is a fair bonus rather than padding. The decoy is handled exactly right: the HS256 branch is named and proven safe at the mechanism level because hash_equals is a constant-time comparator, and crucially alg:none and the hard-coded secret are kept as real Criticals rather than being mislabelled as the decoy, which is the trap many fall into. D2 is strong. The chain is ordered and reconciled to the capture (SQLi 02:15:31, the 312-row exfil, XSS 02:18:47, file read around 02:24:02), the scope change onto the shared /api/v1/internal service is called out, and the BoltCash six-week window and the roughly 63 million naira impact are tied to a stated 20-row sample extrapolation with assumptions, which is exactly what the key rewards. The one technical slip is the SQLi CVSS: it is scored AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H at 9.8, but the auth bypass does not touch availability, so it should be A:N giving roughly 9.1; fix that and tighten the briefer justifications on the XXE and traversal vectors. D3 is the highlight. The executive summary is jargon-free and lands on the customers-and-naira headline, the threat model traces the three trust boundaries, every finding cites a line and a timestamp, the decoy is restated correctly, the earliest-break fix is the parameterised query at the attacker's front door, and remediation is ordered by effort-to-risk with an explicit rationale for placing SQLi ahead of the higher-scoring 10.0 items, not by raw CVSS. The two detection stopgaps each give an exact field (form_username, the legacy_admin_jwt cookie carrying eyJhbGciOiJub25l) and a false-positive rate, which is precisely the ask. D4 answers all four prompts in a clear own voice anchored to the 312 customers and the legacy-admin finding, declines the journalist, scopes what goes in writing, preserves the colleague evidence formally, and treats customer notification as non-negotiable, and it cites ISC2 Canon I load-bearingly. The single gap that holds it back is the NDPA: it states the 72-hour duty and the duty to notify subjects but never names section 40 or section 41, so the legal anchor is generic rather than load-bearing. The most important fix is to cite NDPA 2023 section 40 (notify NDPC within 72 hours) and section 41 (notify the 312 data subjects on high risk) by number, and correct the SQLi vector to A:N.
